title: Cable Sampler
description: Knit a cable sampler swatch that combines a mock rib hem, three classic cable types,  so you can practice planning, crossing, and finishing cables neatly on your machine.
prepChecklist: Choose a smooth, light colored yarn that shows cable texture clearly and works well at a medium tension on your machine.
Gather a contrasting yarn to use later as a decorative cord through the serpentine cable.
Have your cable tools or transfer tools ready for 1 x 1, 2 x 2, and 3 x 3 cable crosses.
Review how to work a mock rib hem on your specific machine model.
Research or choose a serpentine or rope cable motif you want to use for the final panel of the swatch.

modules.title: Cast On and Work the Mock Rib Hem
modules.htmlDescription:
Begin by creating a neat mock rib hem that will anchor the cable sampler.

  1. Cast on 50 stitches (25-0-25) using your preferred mock rib hem setup for this machine.
  2. Knit 20 rows for the hem.
  3. Hang the mock rib hem onto the needles to create a doubled edge.
  4. Knit 6 rows in plain stockinette above the hem so you have a flat surface before the cables begin.

This gives you a tidy lower edge and enough stockinette to highlight the cables that follow.
modules.microQuestion: Is your mock rib hem hanging evenly with 6 smooth rows of stockinette above it and no twisted or missed stitches?

microResponses.yes: Great. A clean hem and smooth base will help your cable sections look intentional and professional.
microResponses.no: Take a moment to adjust or rehang any uneven areas before you continue; fixing the foundation now will improve the whole swatch.

modules.title: Set Up Three Cable Panels with Purl Outlines
modules.htmlDescription:
Now you will position three different cable types across the swatch and frame each one with purl stitches so the texture stands out.

  1. Identify the needle groups for each cable: needles R16 and R17 for a 1 x 1 cable, needles R1 to R4 for a 2 x 2 cable, and needles L12 to L17 for a 3 x 3 cable.
  2. On this setup row, begin working a single purl stitch on each side of every cable panel so each cable is outlined by purl stitches.
  3. Maintain these purl stitches as you knit the cable section so the cables remain clearly framed in the fabric.

Double check that the cable groups sit where you expect them to be across the width and that each one has a purl stitch on both sides.
modules.microQuestion: Are your 1 x 1, 2 x 2, and 3 x 3 cable sections clearly positioned and outlined by a single purl stitch on each side?

microResponses.yes: Excellent. Clear purl outlines will make each cable easy to see and evaluate when the swatch is finished.
microResponses.no: Pause and adjust your needle selection or purl stitches now so each cable panel has a neat, matching outline.

modules.title: Work Repeating Crosses on All Three Cables
modules.htmlDescription:
With the panels set up, you will now work a series of cable crosses to build height and texture.

  1. Knit 4 rows in pattern, keeping the purl outlines in place around each cable.
  2. On the next row, cross each of the three cables using the appropriate transfer method for 1 x 1, 2 x 2, and 3 x 3 cables.
  3. Repeat the sequence of knit 4 rows, then cross all cables a total of 5 times, counting the first set as one repeat.
  4. After the final cross, knit 4 more rows while still maintaining the purl outlines, then end the purl stitches so the fabric returns to plain stockinette.

Keep your tension even and watch that each cross is mirrored correctly so the cables grow in a consistent, rhythmic pattern.
modules.microQuestion: Do the three cable columns show evenly spaced crosses with consistent direction and neat purl outlines from bottom to top?

microResponses.yes: Nice work. Consistent crossings and outlines mean you are managing both your tools and tension well.
microResponses.no: Look for any crosses that twist the wrong way or purl outlines that drift; noting these now will help you correct them in your next cable swatch.

modules.title: Knit the Serpentine Cable Panel and Finish the Swatch
modules.htmlDescription:
To complete the sampler, you will add a serpentine or rope cable that can hold a contrast cord for extra dimension.

  1. After ending the purl outlines, knit 10 rows in plain stockinette across all 50 stitches to separate the first cable section from the serpentine panel.
  2. Over the next 20 rows, work your chosen serpentine or rope cable design somewhere in the fabric, following the chart or plan you researched earlier.
  3. Maintain smooth background stitches so the cable path is easy to see and does not distort the rest of the swatch.
  4. When the serpentine section is complete, knit a final 10 rows of plain stockinette and bind off neatly.
  5. After the swatch is off the machine, twine a contrasting knit cord through the serpentine cable path so the movement of the cable is easy to follow.

This last panel shows how cables can be used decoratively and how a contrast cord can emphasize their shape.
modules.microQuestion: Does your serpentine cable create a clear path that the contrast cord can follow without fighting tight or distorted stitches?

microResponses.yes: Wonderful. A smooth serpentine path with a twined cord makes this sampler both a learning tool and a design idea for future projects.
microResponses.no: Note where the cable feels tight, crowded, or unclear; on your next try, you can widen the cable area, adjust tension, or space the crosses differently.

reflection.question: After completing this cable sampler, do you feel more confident setting up, crossing, and finishing different cable styles on your machine?

responses.yes: That confidence will serve you well. You now have experience with multiple cable types plus a decorative serpentine panel you can adapt to garments and accessories.
responses.no: That is completely fine. Cables are a skill that grows with practice; repeating one section of this sampler or working a simpler cable again can build your comfort step by step.
